questions.q: Where do you sleep at a campsite?
questions.fact: Some tents fold down small enough to fit in a backpack.

questions.q: What helps you see in the dark at camp?
questions.fact: A headlamp lets you keep your hands free.

questions.q: What zips up around you when you sleep outside?
questions.fact: A sleeping bag helps you stay cozy on cool nights.

questions.q: What sweet treat do people toast on a stick?
questions.fact: S'mores are made with marshmallows, chocolate and graham crackers.

questions.q: What do we call the spot where you set up your tent?
questions.fact: Many campsites have a picnic table.

questions.q: What is good to wear on your feet for a hike?
questions.fact: Comfy shoes make a long walk more fun.

questions.q: What do you carry your things in on a hike?
questions.fact: A backpack is easier to carry when the heavy things sit close to your back.

questions.q: What do you use to pound tent pegs into the ground?
questions.fact: Tent pegs help keep your tent from blowing away.

questions.q: What do we call a path through the woods for walking?
questions.fact: Trails are often marked with painted signs or stripes.

questions.q: What twinkles in the night sky when you are far from city lights?
questions.fact: Away from city lights, you can see many more stars.

questions.q: Which of these could you sit on around a campfire?
o: A log or a camp chair
questions.fact: Camp chairs fold up flat to fit in the car.

questions.q: What do you look at to find your way on a hike?
questions.fact: A map is a picture of a place as seen from above.

questions.q: What is a good thing to do with your trash at camp?
o: Put it in a trash bag or bin
questions.fact: Keeping the outdoors clean helps everyone enjoy it.

questions.q: What goes over a tent like an umbrella to keep out rain?
questions.fact: The rainfly goes over the top of the tent and hangs down the sides.

questions.q: In which direction does the Sun rise?
questions.fact: The Sun sets in the west.

questions.q: What tool shows you which way is north?
questions.fact: A compass needle is a little magnet that lines up with Earth's magnetic field.

questions.q: What is a map's key or legend for?
o: It explains what the symbols mean
questions.fact: A key tells you what each little picture on the map stands for.

questions.q: What is a painted mark on a tree that shows a trail called?
questions.fact: Blazes are often painted stripes on trees or rocks.

questions.q: Which star helps people find north in the Northern Hemisphere?
questions.fact: Polaris stays almost still while the other stars seem to circle around it.

questions.q: What does it mean to pitch a tent?
questions.fact: Pitching a tent means getting it ready to sleep in.

questions.q: Why do campers often use a sleeping pad?
o: It cushions and warms you from the ground
questions.fact: The ground is cooler than the air, so a pad adds a layer between you and it.

questions.q: What does GPS stand for?
questions.fact: GPS uses signals from satellites orbiting Earth.

questions.q: What is a trailhead?
o: The place where a trail begins
questions.fact: Trailheads often have a sign or a map.

questions.q: What is a switchback on a mountain trail?
o: A zigzag turn that makes a climb easier
questions.fact: Switchbacks make steep hills gentler to climb.

questions.q: What does a thermometer measure?
questions.fact: Temperature is measured in degrees Celsius or Fahrenheit.

questions.q: What do we call a shelter made of branches leaning against a frame?
questions.fact: A lean-to has a slanted roof and an open front.

questions.q: What is dusk?
o: The time in the evening when daylight is fading
questions.fact: Dawn is the same kind of soft light, but in the morning.

questions.q: What is the band of stars you might see from a dark campsite called?
questions.fact: The Milky Way is our own galaxy seen from the inside.

questions.q: What does the scale on a map help you figure out?
questions.fact: A map scale can say, for example, that one inch is one mile.

questions.q: What do contour lines on a topographic map show?
questions.fact: When lines are close together, the ground is steep.

questions.q: What do we call hiking with your gear on your back and staying out overnight?
questions.fact: Backpackers try to carry as little weight as they can.

questions.q: What does elevation mean on a trail sign?
questions.fact: Sea level is the average height of the ocean's surface.

questions.q: What is a cairn?
o: A pile of stacked stones marking a path
questions.fact: Cairns help hikers find the path above the treeline.

questions.q: What do we call a large area set aside to protect wild land and animals?
questions.fact: Parks help keep wild places and their animals around for the future.

questions.q: If you face east, which direction is behind you?
questions.fact: Facing the morning sun means you are facing east.

questions.q: How many degrees are in a full circle on a compass?
questions.fact: North is 0 degrees, east is 90, south is 180 and west is 270.

questions.q: What do we call the shimmering lights in the far northern sky?
questions.fact: Auroras happen when particles from the Sun hit Earth's atmosphere.

questions.q: What is orienteering?
o: Finding your way with a map and compass
questions.fact: Orienteering began as military training in Sweden.

questions.q: What is the treeline on a tall mountain?
o: The line of trees along a road
The height above which trees cannot grow
questions.fact: Above the treeline it is too cold and windy for trees.

questions.q: Which planet is often seen as a bright evening star near sunset?
questions.fact: Venus is the brightest planet in our night sky.

questions.q: What is the Big Dipper's shape?
questions.fact: Two stars at the end of the Big Dipper's bowl point toward the North Star.

questions.q: What mostly causes ocean tides?
questions.fact: Most coasts have two high tides and two low tides each day.
